text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm drafting the RFC follow-up for pilot shadowing. Proposal: mirror 5% of production inference traffic to the pilot variant (non-blocking) with strict side-effect filtering. Need to converge on fallback criteria, cache warmup, session affinity, and telemetry/billing. Thoughts?

derek: +1 for mirror-only non-blocking. Important: filter out any requests that can cause side-effects (webhooks, DB writes). We can add a header on the mirror path like `X-Mirror: true` and `X-ReadOnly: true`. :eyes: Also prefer async mirror to avoid adding tail latency.

kai: Two things from infra perspective: (1) Mirrored payloads must be pseudonymized (hash user ids) to avoid PII leakage. (2) Pilot will always see cold KV caches — suggest a warmup job that replays high-frequency prefixes to the pilot at low QPS before we increase mirror percent.

sasha: Fallback rules we should codify: auto-disable pilot routing if 95th perc latency > baseline + 200ms for 2 consecutive minutes OR error-rate delta > 1% for 1 minute. When auto-disabled, trigger circuit-breaker, notify #oncall and create an ops incident stub. Cooloff window = 10m before allowing auto-reenable.

deploy-bot: deployment started: `pilot-shadow-v2` deployed to cluster-us-west at 12:34 UTC. Observe metrics at https://console.redwood/runs/428490 (bot message).

maria: Good — also want to define runtime routing flags in the RFC: `mirror_enabled`, `mirror_percent`, `allow_side_effects`, `pilot_warmup_job`, `mirror_anonymize`. We'll put config examples in the doc.

derek: On mirroring mode: async log-only mirror + periodic synchronous sampling for quality checks seems safest. Async mirror avoids latency risk; sampling probes allow us to compare outputs deterministically. Implement periodic sample compare: take N samples/min and synchronously run control+pilot for those samples.

kai: Sample probe idea: pick N = 1000 samples/hour by reservoir sampling from live requests (respecting PII rules), run both control and pilot, compute embedding-based similarity and a token-level diff. If semantic drift > threshold we fire regression alert. We'll need an eval job and storage for diffs.

sasha: Ops runbook: when auto-disable triggers, keep pilot in warm state for 30m to allow debugging traces. Persist probe diffs and attach pre-sampled requests to the incident. Provide a `/replay` shortlink for engineers to run failing samples against debug builds. Manual override toggle for leads should exist but require two approvals.

maria: Billing/telemetry notes: mark mirrored=true in all telemetry so we can distinguish mirrored tokens. Mirror tokens are billable to variant team — recommend a `pilot.mirror.tokens` metric with tags {variant, team}. Also redact or hash any PII before storage.

derek: Cost mitigation: enable token quota on mirror path and a cost cap per variant. If mirror token spend > X% of expected, auto-throttle mirror percent.

kai: Session affinity/state concern: if a live user ever gets routed (non-mirror) to pilot, we must prefer control for subsequent live requests to avoid user-visible divergence. Suggest a runtime flag `sticky_to_control_on_pilot_hit` that marks the session cookie and routes accordingly. For mirror case, we should not flip affinity.

sasha: Edge cases: streaming outputs and function-calls. We should disallow streaming mirroring (too complex) and only mirror final payloads. For function-calls that trigger external side-effects, exclude from mirror. Add a validator in the router to inspect `tools`/`function_call` fields.

maria: Sounds good. I'll draft the RFC follow-up with: config schema, failure thresholds, probe sampling config, warmup job spec, ops playbook, and telemetry/billing contract. Can reviewers ack before EOW?

derek: I can review today.

kai: I'll review too, focus on sampling infra and data retention.

sasha: I'll review ops + runbook parts.

maria: Thanks — I'll post the draft in #eng-architecture and tag reviewers when ready.
